content.text: Through the Canvas: The Life & Work of
Discover the life and work of contemporary artist Aveline Korr, whose bold vision transforms silence and memory into layered visual stories.
Born in 1985, Aveline grew up near abandoned factories and industrial skylines. These raw landscapes became her first sketches and lasting inspiration.
For Aveline, art is not escape but translation — the act of turning fleeting emotions and unspoken moments into textures, colors, and space.
Her early canvases captured concrete walls, rust, and forgotten corners. Each painting echoed the beauty hidden in decay and imperfection.
In 2012, her first solo exhibition marked a turning point. Critics praised her ability to blend intimacy with large-scale urban narratives.
The success of her first exhibitions marked a shift — from promising newcomer to an artist with a distinct, recognizable voice.
Layer upon layer, Aveline builds meaning. Fragmented perspectives and recurring motifs have since become her signature style.
Never bound by medium, Aveline expands into sculpture, digital art, and collaborative performance, challenging what painting can become.
Residencies in Tokyo, Berlin, and Mexico City have shaped her latest series. These works weave global influences into a mature, layered vision that defines her art today.
Her work has been shown in over 30 countries and collected internationally. Awards and critical acclaim continue to affirm her place in the global art scene.
In her studio today, each new canvas begins where the last left off. Discover, collect, or collaborate — the journey is still unfolding.
